Method explainer · October 2026

MouldVision

A three-minute visual contrast test on your own phone, built to be read alongside the air you breathe: a functional measure for mould, indoor air quality, longevity and the exposome.
What it measuresHow faint a striped pattern each eye can still identify, at five bar widths, two eyes, 90 patches.
What it is forA repeatable, non-invasive marker to track over time alongside building assessment and clinical care.
What it is notNot a diagnosis of mould illness, not a biomarker of exposure, and not a substitute for an eye examination.
1 · Why measure vision in an environmental health practice

The exposome needs functional measures, not just lists of exposures

Genes account for a fraction of long-term health. The rest is the exposome: everything a person meets from conception onward, including the air inside the buildings where Australians spend close to ninety per cent of their lives [17, 19]. Measuring that load is the central difficulty of environmental medicine. Air and surface sampling describe the building; blood and urine describe one moment in a body; a functional test describes what the nervous system is doing right now.

Dampness and mould are common and consequential

The World Health Organization's indoor-air guideline treats dampness and mould as a preventable risk to respiratory health, and meta-analyses place the increase in respiratory symptoms among occupants of damp or mouldy homes at roughly 30–50 per cent [18, 20, 21]. Beyond the airways, occupants report fatigue, cognitive and visual complaints that are harder to measure, and it is here that an objective, quick, repeatable test has value.

Contrast sensitivity sits where optics meets the brain

Contrast sensitivity is the ability to see faint differences in shade. It depends on the clarity of the eye's optics and on neural processing in the retina, optic nerve and visual cortex [10, 11]. Because it draws on both, it changes with ageing, cataract, glaucoma and macular disease, and also with agents that act on the nervous system: alcohol, tobacco, lead, solvents and, in a body of work going back to the 1990s, biotoxins from water-damaged buildings and harmful algal blooms [4–8].

The longevity case

Healthspan is shaped by cumulative, low-grade environmental load that no single clinical visit captures. The tests that matter for longevity are the ones people will actually repeat: cheap, short, at home, and sensitive to change. Contrast sensitivity is already an established marker of visual ageing [3, 11]; measured on a phone, it becomes a quarterly data point rather than a once-a-decade clinic measurement.

One marker, honestly framed

Reduced contrast sensitivity is non-specific. On its own it cannot tell a damp house from an early cataract. Its value comes from being tracked over time, in the same person, under recorded conditions, and read alongside what is known about the building and the person. MouldVision is built around that principle: every result carries its conditions, and no result carries a label.

~90 %of time spent indoors in developed-country activity surveys [19]
5 × 9bar widths × contrast levels per eye, the classic FACT / VCTS layout [1, 2]

2 · What the test measures

Five bar widths, nine contrast steps, three tilts

Each patch is a circle of soft, parallel bars on a mid-grey background. The bars are a sine-wave grating faded at the edges by a Gaussian window, the stimulus of record in vision science [2, 10]. Two things vary:

Bar width (spatial frequency). Five columns, A to E, at 1.5, 3, 6, 12 and 18 cycles per degree of visual angle. Column A is coarse; column E is close to the limit of normal acuity. Human sensitivity peaks in the middle, at 3–6 cycles per degree, which is also where the water-damaged-building literature reports deficits [5–8].

Contrast. Nine rows from 28.6 % down to 0.5 % Michelson contrast, spaced evenly on a logarithmic scale, so each step is the same proportional change. Contrast sensitivity is simply the reciprocal: identifying a 2 % patch means a sensitivity of 50.

Tilt. Every patch leans left, stands upright or leans right, by 15°. The person reports the tilt. With three choices, guessing is right one time in three, so the record keeps every answer rather than reducing a column to one number.

Why "cycles per degree" and not pixels

A bar width only means something at a known viewing distance. MouldVision converts pixels to degrees of visual angle from the phone's known pixel density and the measured eye-to-screen distance, so a 6 cpd patch is a 6 cpd patch on any phone.

The five columns at one contrast: 1.5, 3, 6, 12 and 18 cycles per degree. Finer bars need more contrast to be seen.
Column C (6 cpd) down the first six rows of the contrast ladder: 28.6, 17.2, 10.4, 6.3, 3.8 and 2.3 %. Rows seven to nine are fainter still and are marked exploratory in every report, because an ordinary 8-bit screen cannot be assumed to render them faithfully.
The three answers: left, upright, right.

3 · The three-minute test

Hold the phone, cover one eye, tap the tilt, swap eyes

1
Start. One paragraph on what is measured, the three tilts, and a link to why environmental toxin exposure matters to this test. Full (90 patches) or quick protocol.
2
Hold the phone. The front camera estimates eye-to-screen distance from the size of the iris, which is about 11.7 mm in almost every adult. Only the number is kept; no image leaves the phone. A checklist records brightness, colour filters and room light.
3
Cover one eye. Right eye first, usual glasses or contacts on. The first two patches are easy and act as practice.
4
Answer. Tap Left, Upright or Right, or swipe the way the bars lean. Patches get fainter down each column and finer across the columns. The screen is plain mid-grey throughout; distance is tracked between patches.
5
Context (optional). Twelve one-tap questions about the building, exposures, eye history and age band. Stored beside the result and shown back in the report; never used in any calculation.
6
Results. A seven-section report with both eyes' charts, saved on the phone, shareable as PDF or as the full machine-readable record.

4 · Reading the result

Every patch is on the chart, so nothing is hidden behind a score

Right eye. 29 of 45 presented patches identified; 1 answered can't see; 0 not presented; 0 isolated correct responses.
Left eye. 32 of 45 presented patches identified; 0 answered can't see; 0 not presented; 1 isolated correct responses.
Illustrative record generated by the test suite from a simulated observer, not a person. Vertical axis: contrast sensitivity (left) and percent contrast (right), logarithmic. Columns: bar width in cycles per degree.

How to read it

  • Green circle: the tilt was identified. Red circle: it was not; the red tail shows the tilt chosen, the black tail the true tilt. Hollow: not presented (quick protocol stops a column after two misses in a row).
  • Red line: the lowest contrast correctly identified in each column, the familiar contrast sensitivity curve. It is descriptive: each level is shown once, so one lucky or unlucky answer moves it.
  • Amber ring: an isolated correct answer, one with a miss at an easier level, which is more likely to be a guess.
  • Hatched band: rows seven to nine, exploratory until the displayed contrast of those rows has been measured on real phones.

5 · What makes a phone test defensible

The physics is fixed; the conditions are recorded; the claims are small

Stimulus

Sine-wave gratings with Michelson contrast computed in linear luminance through the sRGB transfer function, a Gaussian envelope (σ = 0.42 of the patch radius), a 5° patch, ±15° tilts, ordered dither to reduce quantisation banding. The renderer is version-stamped and has not changed since the first reviewed build; any change restarts the normative sample.

Geometry without a calibration card

Pixel density comes from a table of phone models matched on screen size and pixel ratio. Viewing distance comes from the front camera every 300 ms, using the near-constant diameter of the adult iris; a one-time 40 cm check pins the camera's focal length. Distance is written to every trial, and if it drifts more than 15 % between patches the next patch is redrawn at the new distance and the drift is recorded.

A complete record

Each run stores all 90 trials with the tilt shown, the answer, the latency, the patch size and the distance at the time; the ladder; the device; the software, protocol, stimulus and scoring versions; and a SHA-256 integrity hash over the test definition and responses, so a record can be checked for accidental alteration. The report prints its versions and hash.

Validation stated, not implied

Every report carries three lines: software verification (an automated suite of 47 tests, bound to the exact source that produced the build), physical measurement validation, and clinical validation. Today the second and third read not performed, and will until the display contrast of real phones has been measured and a normative sample exists. The rows that an 8-bit screen cannot be assumed to render are marked exploratory rather than scored.

No labels

The report never says positive, negative, pass, fail or abnormal, and never attributes a result to mould, mycotoxins or any exposure. It describes what was shown, what was answered, and under what conditions; it tells people when an eye examination is warranted; and it directs questions about a building to building assessment.

The evidence on VCS and water-damaged buildings, briefly

A NIOSH study found lower contrast sensitivity at every bar width among staff of a severely water-damaged school than at a comparison school, yet advised against using VCS to evaluate mould-exposed people because the earlier literature was confounded and poorly controlled [12]. A 2026 comparison found the handheld chart did not separate exposed people from controls while digital tests did, and called the digital tools investigational [13]. Toxicology and infectious-disease bodies state that no validated biomarker or diagnostic test for mould-related illness exists [14, 15]. MouldVision takes the position those papers point to: build the digital instrument carefully, collect the data properly, and claim nothing until it has.

6 · The research programme and how to take part

From a measurement to a reference range

"Normal" for MouldVision will be a measured distribution, not a formula borrowed from a chart printed in 1984. Until it exists, the only comparison the app makes is each person against their own earlier runs.

Phase A — colleagues and existing BHS clients (now)

People who have had a BHS building assessment or mail-order mould test are invited to run the test on their own phone, repeat it 2–14 days later under the same conditions, and, if they choose, send the de-identified record to the research dashboard with the environmental questionnaire. The kit or job number links a vision record to a measured building without any name travelling with it.

Phase B — a normative sample

Target 150 adults aged 18–75 with no known eye disease, wearing their usual correction, across at least three phone models, each tested twice. Outputs: per-column 5th–95th percentile bands by age band, test–retest limits of agreement (the test's own noise), and device effects. Ethics approval precedes any recruitment beyond colleagues.

Phase C — the exposome dataset

Vision records read alongside spore-trap, tape-lift and settle-plate results for the same address, questionnaire context, and, where clinicians take part, their own patients' codes. Descriptive cross-tabulations first; any model later, pre-registered.

What we ask of a participant

  • A phone made in the last eight years, brightness at maximum, in a normally lit room.
  • Three minutes per eye, twice, a week or two apart.
  • Optional: the twelve context questions, and consent to send the de-identified record.

What we promise

  • No name, email, address or date of birth is collected by the app. Camera frames are processed on the phone and never stored or sent.
  • Records sent to research are identified by a six-character code only, can be withdrawn by quoting the run ID, and are never used to compute a classification.
  • Participants keep their own PDF and full record, and a copy of whatever the dataset eventually shows.

Where it lives

visualcontrastsensitivity.com, installable from the browser on iPhone and Android, working offline after the first visit. The source is version-controlled and every build is tied to the test results that verified it.

Concept and scientific lead: Dr Cameron Jones, PhD, Principal Environmental Microbiologist.

MouldVision is a screening and research instrument. It does not diagnose any condition, does not detect mould or mycotoxins in a person, and is not a substitute for an eye examination or medical advice. Questions about a building are answered by environmental assessment; questions about health by a medical practitioner. Software verification status, measurement validation status and clinical validation status are printed on every report. This document describes the method as built in October 2026 (v0.8.0) and will be revised as the validation work reports.
